adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Init() was reordered so the search index initialization (s.search.init(ctx)) runs *before* starting the watcher (s.initWatcher()). Previously the watcher was started first. If search.init performs a snapshot/build of state (e.g., via stats/reads) and relies on watcher events to cover concurrent writes, this new ordering creates a clear window where writes committed during index build occur before the watch subscription exists and therefore won’t be delivered to handleEvent. The diff shows no follow-up reconciliation after initWatcher to backfill missed events, so a silently stale index is a plausible real defect introduced by this change.

This can therefore block server construction/startup. However, the finding’s claim that the ctx is an "un-deadlined background ctx" (no timeout/cancellation) is not directly verifiable from the provided diff because the definition/origin of `ctx` inside `NewResourceServer` is not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Removing the lock around the whole BuildIndex lets concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same key build duplicate indexes (bleve.New on the same file dir fails/conflicts) and last-writer-wins overwrites the cache, leaking the other index.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex used to hold cacheMu for the entire function; the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` (new lock/unlock at end). BuildIndex creates a file-backed index at a deterministic directory path derived from `key` (`filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))`). With the coarse lock removed, concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` can run simultaneously and attempt `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same path, potentially conflicting, and whichever finishes last will overwrite `b.cache[key]`, leaving the other built index untracked/unused. The diff itself shows the reduced synchronization and shared-dir creation, so this concurrency hazard is introduced/exposed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:199 — Search watcher subscribes to WatchWriteEvents only after the index build completes, so writes committed between the list/stats snapshot and subscription are silently missed from the index (and startup now takes longer, widening the gap).

adjudication.rationale: The diff reorders initialization in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go: Init() now runs s.search.init(ctx) (which builds the search index) before starting s.initWatcher() (the change-watching mechanism). Previously, the watcher was started first. Since search indexing also has an event handler (handleEvent) meant to process write events, delaying watcher startup until after the full index build creates a window where writes occurring during startup/build will not be observed/processed by the watcher, potentially leaving the index stale. Moving Init() to NewResourceServer (and removing per-RPC Init calls) further centralizes this longer startup window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:319 — With per-request Init checks removed, Stop setting s.initErr no longer rejects requests, so calls after shutdown proceed against a stopped backend instead of failing fast.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls removed from handlers and an eager `s.Init(ctx)` added in `NewResourceServer`, but it does not show `Stop` or any logic where `Stop` sets `s.initErr` and `Init` would then reject subsequent requests. Since the claimed shutdown-path behavior is not present/visible in the diff, the finding cannot be verified from these changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:309 — Moving the server watcher after search init delays the broadcaster until the index build finishes and any search init error now aborts server construction entirely, making search index failures fatal to all storage operations.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move `initWatcher()` to run after `s.search.init(ctx)` inside `server.Init` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), which can delay starting the watcher/broadcaster until after the (potentially long) search index initialization completes. The diff also makes `NewResourceServer` call `s.Init(ctx)` and return an error if it fails, so a search init failure can now prevent server construction entirely. However, prior to this change, most RPC methods called `s.Init(ctx)` and would have failed on the first operation anyway if init/search init failed, so the claim that this newly makes search failures “fatal to all storage operations” overstates what the diff proves; it’s primarily an initialization/availability coupling and startup-order concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:189 — errgroup workers assign the shared outer err and increment totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization, a data race now exercised on the startup-critical path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any errgroup usage, shared outer `err` variable, or a `totalBatchesIndexed` counter in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` around the referenced line. The only visible changes in `search.go` are switching tracer `Start` to capture `ctx`, adding an info log after initialization, and swapping `logger.Warn` for `s.log.Warn`. While `server.go` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` during `NewResourceServer`, the specific claimed data race is not verifiable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:260 — Init failure is logged twice (inside Init and again in NewResourceServer).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an Init() call in NewResourceServer() that logs on error (`s.log.Error("error initializing resource server", ...)`), while Init() itself already logs the same message when `s.initErr != nil` inside the `s.initOnce.Do` block. So an Init failure will be logged once in Init and again in NewResourceServer, causing duplicate error logs. This is a real, diff-grounded issue but not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — Postgres skip landed alongside a change to startup Init ordering and failure paths, so a real postgres startup regression could be hidden by the only integration test that boots the storage server

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a Postgres-only skip in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (`if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip(...) }`), reducing integration coverage for Postgres. In the same PR, resource server startup/init behavior changes materially: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and fails fast on init errors, and init ordering in `Init` is changed (search init before watcher) while per-RPC `Init` calls are removed. That combination makes it a specific, diff-grounded concern that a Postgres startup regression related to the new init/failure paths could go undetected in CI because this test will no longer run for Postgres.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Moving Init into NewResourceServer (constructor now fails on backend/search/watcher init errors and blocks on the full index build) has no test for the error return, the watcher-after-search ordering, or requests arriving after construction

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a substantive behavior change: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on init failure (server.go adds init at ~255-262), while all per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc). `Init` also changes ordering to initialize the search index before starting the watcher (moved `initWatcher()` after `s.search.init(ctx)` around ~294-313). The PR diff adds no corresponding tests for: constructor error propagation, the watcher-after-search ordering, or the fact requests no longer self-init if a server is constructed/used differently. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test/behavior-coverage concern rather than a directly verifiable defect.

The claim about a context/goroutine leak and missing test coverage for that path cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Narrowing cacheMu to just the map write allows concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key (and GetIndex reads during a build) with no concurrency or -race test covering the last-writer-wins behavior

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go BuildIndex, the diff removes the cacheMu lock that previously covered the entire function (including index creation/build) and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This clearly allows concurrent BuildIndex executions to proceed in parallel and potentially build multiple indexes for the same `key`, with the cache ending up last-writer-wins. Whether `GetIndex` reads are protected isn’t shown in this diff, so a concrete data race can’t be verified here, but the concurrency/behavior change is real and nontrivial and is not covered by anything in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:187 — init now runs parallel builds with the propagated span ctx, but the shared err and totalBatchesIndexed variables are written from errgroup goroutines, and no race-detector test exercises this startup path

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` only changes span context capture (`ctx, span := ...`), swaps logging to `s.log`, and adds an info log after init. It does show a goroutine in `init` (the `}()` hunk), but there is no diff evidence of `errgroup` usage or shared variables like `err`/`totalBatchesIndexed` being written from multiple goroutines, nor any newly introduced parallel build logic. The finding cites a race on variables that are not present in the shown changes, so it cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:452 — Removing per-request Init calls from every RPC leaves no test confirming that handlers work without lazy init (for example, servers built by struct literal or mocks)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls from many handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` once in `NewResourceServer` (returning error if init fails). This changes the contract: callers must construct the server via `NewResourceServer` (or otherwise ensure `Init` is called). The finding’s point—there’s no test in this diff that exercises handlers when the server is not lazily initialized anymore (e.g., constructed via struct literal/mocks)—is a specific, change-induced test/contract concern grounded in the removal of lazy init, not a directly provable functional defect from the diff alone.
